reason: Conversation 2 asks a sensible clarifying question, quickly reaches the correct conclusion that this is a normal anti-crease phase, and does not push unnecessary repair or an engineer. It does wrongly claim the feature cannot be disabled without specialist service, when the manual may cover switching it off, but this is minor. Conversation 1 opens with alarmist fire and safety warnings and lists timer, control board and relay faults, which are unsupported claims. It also uses US units, dollars and North American voltage for a UK user, suggests unplugging or flipping the breaker, and mentions hidden button holds and lifting the top cover with screws. It does eventually identify the anti-crease behaviour and points to the manual, but it is long, repetitive and sends the user hunting for the model number when simply reading the manual they already have would have worked.
